thesis: Sabine Royalty Trust is a Texas express trust that holds non-operating royalty and mineral interests across producing and proved undeveloped oil and gas properties in Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas. **[Fact]** The Trust has no employees; Argent Trust Company serves as trustee and distributes essentially all distributable income monthly. **[Fact]** As of February 27, 2026, there were **14,579,345** units outstanding (`SBR/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260227_rpt20251231_acc0001193125_26_081251.htm`). **[Fact]** Calendar Q1 2026 royalty income was **$14.19 million** and distributable income was **$13.04 million** ($0.89 per unit for the quarter) with cash and short-term investments of **$8.26 million** at March 31, 2026 (`SBR/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260508_rpt20260331_acc0001193125_26_213810.htm`). **[Fact]** The May 2026 monthly distribution was **$0.497900** per unit (`SBR/investor-documents/sec-edgar/8-K_20260505_exhibit_sbr-ex99_1.htm_acc0001193125_26_205699.htm`).
why_market_wrong: Yield-oriented screens often skip royalty trusts, K-1 complexity, and depletion narrative, so a long record of cash distributions can trade below a simple sum of expected payouts. **[Inference]** Horizon Kinetics frames Sabine as a localized inflation beneficiary: monthly pass-through of oil and gas prices with minimal overhead (~0.7% of revenues in their commentary). **[Inference]** Engineering has added proved reserves over decades despite production, which the market may under-weight when pricing the trust on near-term distribution noise alone.
